title: Start sub-system build
description: The requirements brief for one working sub-system, worked out from real-world scenarios and the admin's answers. A background build designs the business flows from it, then the entities, a page for every journey step, the processing each submit needs, and launches the journeys.

domain.description: The business area. An existing domain of the same name is reused.

name.description: Name of the business area, for example Venue Bookings.

description.description: One sentence on what the area covers.

summary.description: What the sub-system does for the organisation and what the admin asked for, in a short paragraph.

people.description: Every kind of person who takes part: staff, the people the domain serves, visitors.

name.description: What they are called, for example Member or Bookings staff.

x-enum-descriptions.admin: Staff of the organisation, working on everyone's records.
x-enum-descriptions.member: People the domain serves who sign in to their own records.
x-enum-descriptions.public: People the domain serves who never sign in, or visitors before they sign up.

description.description: What they do in the scenarios.

sign_in.description: For the people the domain serves: whether they sign in and how their accounts are made. Only what the admin confirmed; logins can't be undone.

x-enum-descriptions.none: They never sign in; staff keep their records.
x-enum-descriptions.self_signup: They sign themselves up on a public page.
x-enum-descriptions.staff_created: Staff create their accounts when adding them.
x-enum-descriptions.both: They sign themselves up, and staff can also create accounts.

scenarios.description: The real-world use cases the sub-system must handle, each with what can go wrong.

name.description: Short name, for example Member books a venue.

actor.description: Who starts it, as named in people.

steps.description: The normal path, in order, including what staff do in between.

items.description: One step of the normal path.

exceptions.description: What can go wrong and how the system responds, such as no seats left, a duplicate request or a failed payment.

rules.description: Business rules: limits, calculations, statuses, who may do what.

items.description: One business rule in plain words.

values.description: Values the admin gave, such as email recipients or web addresses, copied exactly. Never invent one, and never include a password, token or secret.

label.description: What the value is, for example Bookings team email.

value.description: The value exactly as the admin wrote it.

not_covered.description: What the platform cannot do or the admin left out, such as reminders sent later or steps that need a password, token or secret.

items.description: One thing that is not covered.

domain.name: Venue Bookings
domain.description: Members book the club's venues; staff approve; members pay.

examples.summary: Members sign up, request a venue for a date and pay once staff approve. Staff review each request and approve or decline it.

scenarios.name: Member books a venue
steps: Picks a venue, a date and the number of guests
Staff approve or decline the request
Pays the venue's daily rate once approved
exceptions: More guests than the venue holds: the request is refused
Payment fails: the booking stays approved and can be paid again

rules: A booking's total is the venue's daily rate.
not_covered: Reminder emails before the booking date
